title: CLI, subcommands, slash commands, dashboard backend, ACP
tldr: Slash commands have no surface-independent layer: each is a printing method on HermesCLI, GatewayRunner mixins, TUI builtins (+ a shadow HermesCLI subprocess), or ACP _cmd_*; /help exists 4 times and TUI /model runs twice in two processes.
Biggest kill: the TUI slash worker (persistent HermesCLI subprocess per session) and its _SLASH_MIRRORS side-effect replay.
Biggest simplification: finish slash_exec.EXECUTORS (6/102 commands) so every CommandDef owns one executor returning a typed reply + effects; ~26 hand lists and 4 handler hosts collapse (~5k lines).
hermes_cli is 260k lines because only 23% is CLI; 31% is core library imported by agent/tools/gateway and 36% is servers/services.

findings.title: Slash commands are methods on four surface objects; no surface-independent command layer
findings.problem: Each slash command is a printing method on whichever surface object first needed it: HermesCLI (78 handler methods), GatewayRunner mixins (62 handlers, gateway/slash_commands*.py = 4,571 lines), TUI _SLASH_BUILTINS + _LIVE_SLASH_OUTPUT formatters, ACP _cmd_* (9). TUI/Desktop run CLI commands by spawning a persistent HermesCLI subprocess per session (the 'shadow CLI', cli_model_switch_mixin.py:262), scraping its Rich output, and replaying mutations onto the live agent via _SLASH_MIRRORS, so /model runs switch_model twice in two processes and each session can carry a second MCP fleet (methods_tools.py:1163). /help has 4 implementations; /queue, /steer, /compress 3-4. Every fix must find its twins (gist: 'missed sibling path' = largest rework class, 56 tags). The right shape exists twice in-repo (goal_command.dispatch_goal_command; slash_exec.EXECUTORS) but covers 6 of 102 commands.
findings.move: Make CommandDef executable: CommandDef.run = 'module:function' implementing run(ctx: CommandContext) -> CommandReply. CommandContext carries args plus a SessionPort protocol each surface implements once (agent, session_db, config, profile_scope(), is_running). CommandReply = text + data + typed effects (SwitchModel, QueueTurn, RebuildAgent, ExitRepl, ClearScreen, OpenPicker). CLI process_command, gateway _command_handler_table, TUI command.dispatch/slash.exec and ACP _handle_slash_command each become resolve -> busy policy from registry -> run -> render/apply effects. Delete slash_worker.py, _SlashWorker, _SLASH_MIRRORS, _PENDING_INPUT_COMMANDS, _WORKER_BLOCKED_COMMANDS, _SLASH_BUILTINS, ACP _cmd_*, gateway handler bodies as commands migrate; mutating commands first (model, compress, queue, steer, new).

reference.pattern: Command = data + callback supplied by a Provider (system_commands.py:19); the palette only renders/invokes

findings.risk: Facade monkeypatch seams on cli.HermesCLI._handle_* and gateway mixins move to executors. Preserve deferred vs --now cache invalidation, per-surface busy semantics, off-turn profile scope binding (methods_slash.py:494, #122655), compute-host forwarding, prompt_toolkit pickers (as OpenPicker effects).

findings.title: ~26 hand-written slash-name collections restate COMMAND_REGISTRY data and have drifted
findings.problem: hermes_cli/AGENTS.md calls COMMAND_REGISTRY the single source; an AST scan finds ~26 parallel collections of command names (gateway _PLAIN_COMMANDS 22 / _IDLE_COMMANDS 35 / busy tables; TUI _PENDING_INPUT_COMMANDS, _TUI_HIDDEN, _TUI_EXTRA, _MUTATES_WHILE_RUNNING; ACP _COMMANDS, _MID_TURN_BLOCKED_COMMANDS). 'Blocked mid-turn' is defined 4 ways. Drift: ACP accepts /reset but not canonical /new, lacks /compact, advertises cli_only /tools, /queue only appends; _SLASH_DISPATCH['exit'] is unreachable. Surface visibility uses 7 mechanisms (cli_only, gateway_only, gateway_config_gate, desktop, desktop_subcommands, _TUI_HIDDEN, _TUI_EXTRA).
findings.move: Replace cli_only/gateway_only/desktop/_TUI_HIDDEN with CommandDef.surfaces: frozenset[Surface]; move _TUI_EXTRA into the registry. Derive gateway _PLAIN_COMMANDS and busy tables from busy_policy/busy_handler, ACP list from surfaces, ACP/TUI blocking from busy_policy=='reject'. One invariant test: every dispatch-table name resolves to a registry entry visible on that surface. Delete 'exit' key.

findings.title: argparse tree: 6 registration conventions, per-group string re-dispatch, main.py forward shims, console re-description
findings.problem: Groups join `hermes` six ways (subcommands build_X_parser + main.cmd_X; register_cli(parent); build_parser().set_defaults; portal add_parser; register_send_subparser / lsp register_subparser; plugin dict descriptors + a separate memory-plugin path). console_engine re-describes 27 families as _CliSurface kinds with hand-typed subcommand lists and '*' mutating markers plus _BLOCKED_TOP/_BLOCKED_PAIRS. Inside groups the chosen leaf is stored as dest='<group>_action' (56 sites) and re-dispatched through per-module dicts (52 getattr sites), which is why AGENTS.md needs the alias-dest rule. main.py holds 24 _forward_command closures + 16 cmd_* only to inject handlers. A new subcommand touches 3-5 files with no check that they agree.
findings.move: One convention: each command module exports register(subparsers) and sets set_defaults(func='module:attr') on every leaf (resolved at call time: keeps laziness and patch seams). Delete <group>_action dicts and _forward_command. Console metadata on the parser (set_defaults(_console='read'|'mutating'|'blocked')); console_engine walks the real tree. Plugins get one register_commands(subparsers) hook (memory plugins included).

reference.pattern: register_commands(cli) hook called once (llm/cli.py:4107); subgroups via @cli.group (llm/cli.py:1543)

findings.risk: register_cli_command(name, help, setup_fn, handler_fn) is plugin API: keep as adapter. --help order = registration order (main.py:3454). Tests patching hermes_cli.main.cmd_X need new targets.

findings.title: Operations print, prompt and sys.exit instead of returning results; other surfaces scrape stdout or spawn the CLI
findings.problem: TUI/Desktop get slash output by scraping a subprocess Rich console; dashboard /api/console runs argparse handlers under redirect_stdout and maps SystemExit codes; dashboard gateway verbs spawn `hermes gateway <verb>`. backup.run_import (CC 56, 321 lines) interleaves validation, restore loop, overwrite prompt, ~60 prints and 5 sys.exit, so no other surface can call it. 17 redirect_stdout sites across hermes_cli + tui_gateway. Scraped text cannot carry structured warnings, so every new surface re-pays this.
findings.move: Split each operation into do_X(...) -> XReport (frozen dataclass, typed errors, no stdout) and a CLI renderer print_X(report). First: backup.run_import -> restore_backup(zip, target, *, overwrite) -> RestoreReport (prompt moves to the CLI caller); gateway start/stop/status callable in-process by the dashboard (subprocess kept only for update, which replaces code); console handlers once CLI-03 gives them leaf functions.

findings.title: Dashboard backend reimplements domain operations per router, against private helpers, in router + web_server_<domain> pairs
findings.problem: 284 routes in 24 routers + 17 web_server_* helpers (~25k lines). Sharing happens only at the bottom (SessionDB, load/save_config, switch_model, profiles.create_profile). Config set has 3 algorithms (dashboard whole-doc merge, CLI set_config_value, TUI per-key setters). Routers import private names (_find_all_skills, _save_platform_tools, _save_mcp_server, _remove_mcp_server) and reach upward into tui_gateway.mcp_rpc_helpers. MCP 409 ownership check is pasted twice; cron validation duplicates the cronjob tool. Each domain is split across web_routers/<d>.py and web_server_<d>.py. 0 response_model=, 148 `except Exception`.
findings.move: One public service function per operation in the owning domain module (config.apply_config_patch(patch, *, scope) -> ConfigChange used by dashboard, `config set`, TUI config.set; mcp_config.add_server/remove_server with the ownership check inside). Routers = parse -> call -> serialize with response_model=. Fold web_server_<d>.py into its router or the domain service. Move server_configs_with_sources into mcp_config.

findings.title: hermes_cli is the core library and four servers; only 23% of its 260k lines is CLI code
findings.problem: CLI proper (interactive CLI, command framework, setup wizard, migrations) is 60,084 lines. 81k lines are libraries other packages import at runtime (config imported by 239 outside files, plugins 57, profiles 47, observability 47, auth 44, models 39, runtime_provider 37); 93k are servers/services (dashboard 31.7k, updater 20.2k, kanban 15.3k, gateway service mgmt 14.7k, desktop host 9.9k, proxy 1.5k). Import matrix: agent->hermes_cli 41/420, tools->hermes_cli 39/266 edges. Path no longer says where code runs; hermes_cli/AGENTS.md (24k chars) must cover unrelated systems.
findings.move: Move by topic, one package per PR, no shims: hermes_dashboard/ (web_server*, web_routers, dashboard_auth, main_dashboard, dashboard_procs, console_engine); kanban/ (kanban_db*, dispatcher + tools/kanban_tools.py + plugins/kanban); gateway/service/ (gateway.py, gateway_launchd/windows/migrate/enroll); hermes_update/; hermes_observability/. config/auth/profiles/providers belong to seams 01/05/07. hermes_cli keeps main, subcommands, commands*, cli_*, setup, doctor.

findings.title: Eager full-tree parser forces four hand-rolled argv fast paths and a hand-kept builtin list
findings.problem: main.py imports 61 builder modules at module level and builds all 426 nodes (~140ms per main.py:3247). main() first tries 4 fast paths that re-derive the chat/serve decision from argv and repeat preconditions (container routing x3, --yolo x3). Divergence caused #105892 (-z ignored --resume). _BUILTIN_SUBCOMMANDS is a 'keep in sync' copy of top-level names used only to decide plugin discovery.
findings.move: One lazy COMMANDS: dict[name, 'module:register'] table; build only the selected group's subparser (all groups only for --help/completion). _BUILTIN_SUBCOMMANDS = COMMANDS.keys(). Fast paths collapse into the now-cheap normal path. Container routing and --yolo run once before parsing.
findings.risk: Startup on Termux/Windows is why fast paths exist: measure cold hermes, hermes serve, hermes --tui before/after. bpo-9338 workaround needs all names (table provides them).

findings.title: HermesCLI is one namespace spread over 17 mixins (627 methods, 241 attributes)
findings.problem: 17 bases, 627 methods, 241 instance attributes (159 assigned in cli_init_mixin). Mixins read each other's attributes and siblings late-import the facade 263 times (`from cli import`) to keep patch seams; mutable state must stay in cli.py by rule. The split spread a class across files without narrowing any interface. HermesCLI doubles as the TUI's slash host (CLI-01), so REPL concerns and command logic cannot separate.
findings.move: After CLI-01, command mixins (commands, loops, info, session, model_switch, billing; ~7.5k lines) become registry executors over SessionPort. HermesCLI keeps prompt_toolkit concerns (tui, status bar, stream, modal, terminal input, voice), promoted to composed objects with explicit deps (StatusBar(state), StreamRenderer(console)).

seam_answer: There are four command languages: the argparse tree (72 top-level commands, 426 nodes), the slash registry (102 commands), the dashboard REST/WS surface (284 routes), and ACP's own 9 slash commands; the dashboard also runs a fifth (console_engine, a curated argparse re-wrap). None is a single source. argparse is restated by _BUILTIN_SUBCOMMANDS, 40 main.py handler shims, ~52 per-group action dicts, _AGENT_COMMANDS/_AGENT_SUBCOMMANDS and console_engine's _CLI_FAMILIES/_BLOCKED_* (~8 lists). Slash commands are named by the registry plus ~26 hand collections across CLI, gateway, TUI and ACP, and implemented up to 4 times (in the TUI via a shadow HermesCLI subprocess). Dashboard routes use neither registry and reimplement domain operations against private helpers. A click-style argparse rewrite alone saves ~1.2k lines (CLI-03, CLI-07). The large win is making CommandDef executable: one run(ctx) -> CommandReply with typed effects per command and one SessionPort per surface deletes the slash worker, mirrors, ACP list, gateway handler tuples and most duplicated handler bodies (~5k lines) plus the twin-not-fixed bug class (CLI-01, CLI-02). The dashboard should call the same domain service functions as the CLI, not the slash registry (CLI-04, CLI-05). hermes_cli is 260k lines because it is also the core library and four servers; only 23% is CLI (CLI-06).
